title: Reddit’s new Rules Hub uses AI to enforce moderation by intent, not keywords. Automod’s other features stay.
excerpt: Reddit's Rules Hub uses LLMs to replace Automod's enforcement workflows. Other Automod features remain. Old Reddit faces changes but Reddit is exploring options.
content_html:
TL;DR

Reddit’s Rules Hub uses LLMs to replace Automod’s enforcement workflows, not Automod itself. Old Reddit faces changes but is not being killed. 130M daily users, 100K+ communities.

Reddit announced a new suite of moderation tools that will eventually replace Automod’s enforcement capabilities, not Automod itself. The centrepiece is Rules Hub, which uses large language models to evaluate whether posts and comments match the intent of a community rule. Together with newer systems called Post & Comment Guidance and Safety Filters, it will take over the enforcement workflows that communities currently rely on Automod to handle. Rules Hub has been testing in over 700 communities and will now be available to all newly created ones.

The platform is also restricting public API access further. Third-party apps must transition to Reddit’s Developer Platform, and new API requests will be gradually restricted. Reddit launched a $1 million migration programme to help developers move. This follows the 2023 API pricing changes that killed popular third-party apps like Apollo and triggered a site-wide protest. The new restrictions complete that transition: all trusted automation will eventually run within Reddit’s own ecosystem.

Old Reddit, the legacy desktop interface, will require login in the short term while Reddit explores further changes. The company said it needs to make changes to protect the platform, business, and users, but is exploring different options and does not have a hard timeline. CEO Steve Huffman also mentioned the possibility of recreating Old Reddit’s UI on the modern foundation. Google replaced its traditional search with AI summaries and faced a backlash from users who preferred the old version. Reddit appears to be treading more carefully, promising to work directly with moderators, developers, and communities before making changes.

Reddit now has over 130 million daily visitors across 100,000+ communities. The key distinction is that only Automod’s enforcement tools are being replaced. All other Automod capabilities remain, and Reddit said it will not change any existing enforcement workflows until replacements are tested and proven in partnership with moderators. If Rules Hub works as described, moderators set rules in plain language and the AI enforces them contextually, reducing the regex-writing and keyword-list maintenance that Automod’s enforcement required. Wharton researchers found people accept AI outputs 80% of the time, and the question for Reddit is whether moderators will trust an LLM to interpret their rules correctly.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Reddit 的规则中心使用 LLM 来取代 Automod 的执行工作流程，而不是 Automod 本身。 旧版 Reddit 面临着变化，但并没有被消灭。 1.3 亿日常用户，10 万+ 社区。

Reddit 宣布推出一套新的审核工具，最终将取代 Automod 的执行功能，而不是 Automod 本身。 核心是规则中心，它使用大型语言模型来评估帖子和评论是否符合社区规则的意图。 与名为“发布和评论指南”和“安全过滤器”的新系统一起，它将接管社区目前依赖 Automod 处理的执行工作流程。 Rules Hub 已在 700 多个社区进行测试，现在将可供所有新创建的社区使用。

该平台还进一步限制公共 API 访问。 第三方应用程序必须过渡到Reddit的开发者平台，并且新的API请求将逐渐受到限制。 Reddit 启动了一项价值 100 万美元的迁移计划来帮助开发者迁移。 在此之前，2023 年 API 定价变化导致 Apollo 等流行第三方应用程序失效，并引发了全站抗议。 新的限制完成了这一转变：所有可信的自动化最终都将在 Reddit 自己的生态系统中运行。

旧版 Reddit 是传统的桌面界面，短期内将需要登录，而 Reddit 正在探索进一步的变化。 该公司表示，需要做出改变以保护平台、业务和用户，但正在探索不同的选择，并且没有硬性的时间表。 首席执行官 Steve Huffman 还提到了在现代基础上重新创建旧 Reddit 用户界面的可能性。 谷歌用人工智能摘要取代了传统搜索，但遭到了喜欢旧版本的用户的强烈反对。 Reddit 似乎行事更加谨慎，承诺在做出改变之前直接与版主、开发者和社区合作。

Reddit 目前每天有超过 1.3 亿访问者，遍布 100,000 多个社区。 关键区别在于，仅 Automod 的执行工具被替换。 所有其他 Automod 功能均保留，Reddit 表示，在与版主合作测试和验证替代方案之前，不会改变任何现有的执行工作流程。 如果规则中心按照描述的方式工作，主持人会用简单的语言设置规则，人工智能会根据上下文强制执行这些规则，从而减少 Automod 执行所需的正则表达式编写和关键字列表维护。 沃顿商学院的研究人员发现，人们在 80% 的情况下接受人工智能输出，而 Reddit 的问题是版主是否会相信法学硕士能够正确解释他们的规则。
